title: Feelings & support
goal: Cheer up a friend who's down, say sorry like you mean it, congratulate someone and offer condolences, using 'while', 'as soon as' and 'until'.
intro:
Friends don't only make plans together — they have bad days, fail exams, break up, lose people they love and get great news. This unit gives you the words to be there for them: asking what's wrong (**किन उदास छौ?**), comforting (**टेन्सन नलेऊ**, **म तिम्रो साथमा छु**), apologising sincerely (**मबाट गल्ती भयो**), congratulating (**पास भएकोमा बधाई छ!**) and offering condolences.

The grammar is about time and feeling: 'while', 'as soon as' and 'until' (**नभएसम्म** — with a surprising न), feelings that happen to you (**तिम्रो याद आयो** 'I missed you') and **-एकोमा** 'for having…' in sorry, thanks and congratulations. Most of it is in the तिमी form you use with friends.

grammar.title: While, as soon as, until: -दा, -ने बित्तिकै, न-…-एसम्म
grammar.body:
Three kinds of time clause help you talk about feelings as they happen. All of them are **verb endings**, not separate words like English 'while' or 'until', and the clause they make comes **before** the main sentence.

**While / when: -दा** (from unit 20). Stem + दा: सुन्**दा** 'when (I) heard', घर जाँ**दा** 'on the way home', म बिरामी हुँ**दा** 'when I was ill'. In relaxed speech people often say **-दाखेरि**: सुन्दाखेरि. To say 'at the time when', use **-एको बेला**: म बिरामी भएको **बेला**.

**As soon as: -ने बित्तिकै** or **-नासाथ**. नतिजा आउ**ने बित्तिकै** 'as soon as the results come', घर पुग्**नासाथ** 'the moment I get home'. **तुरुन्तै** 'right away' often goes in the main clause.

**Until: न- + -एसम्म.** Nepali says 'until' as 'as long as … has *not* happened': तिमी निको **नभएसम्म** 'until you get better' (lit. as long as you haven't got well), ऊ **नआएसम्म** पर्ख 'wait until he comes'. The -ए- is the same stem as in -एको: गरेसम्म, खाएसम्म, आएसम्म, and irregular **गएसम्म** (जानु), **भएसम्म** (हुनु).

The trap: English speakers drop the न. Without it, **भएसम्म** means 'as long as': म यहाँ **भएसम्म** 'as long as I'm here'. Careful speech also uses **जबसम्म … तबसम्म** 'as long as … (so long)', and you will hear **-उन्जेल** in the same sense as न-…-एसम्म: ऊ नआउन्जेल 'until he comes'.

grammar.title: Feelings that happen to you — and feelings you cause
grammar.body:
Unit 14 showed feelings that 'strike' you (मलाई डर लाग्यो). Nepali takes this further: many emotional events simply **happen** to you, and the grammar shows it.

**Missing someone: याद आउनु.** Literally 'the memory (of X) comes (to me)': मलाई तिम्रो **याद आयो** 'I missed you', मलाई घरको याद आउँछ 'I miss home'. The person who feels it takes **-लाई**, the person or thing missed takes **-को**, and the verb agrees with याद — so it is always **आयो / आउँछ**, never आएँ or आउँछु.

**Other feelings that happen:** मलाई **नरमाइलो लाग्यो** 'I felt bad / it was a shame' · मलाई **एक्लो महसुस भयो** 'I felt lonely' · मलाई **टेन्सन भयो** 'I got stressed'. **मन** 'heart' can be the subject: मेरो **मन दुख्यो** 'I was hurt', मन **हल्का भयो** 'I feel lighter, relieved'.

**Mistakes happen 'from' you:** **मबाट गल्ती भयो** 'a mistake happened from me' is the natural, sincere apology. मैले गल्ती गरेँ 'I made a mistake' is also correct but sounds blunter. Pronoun + बाट: मबाट, तिमीबाट, उसबाट, हामीबाट.

**Making someone feel something: the causative -आउनु.** दुख्नु 'to hurt (by itself)' → **दुखाउनु** 'to hurt (someone)'; रुनु 'to cry' → **रुवाउनु** 'to make cry'; हाँस्नु 'to laugh' → **हँसाउनु** 'to make laugh'. The causative has an object, so in the past the causer takes **ले**: तिमी**ले** मलाई हँसायौ 'you made me laugh'. The plain verb takes no ले: मेरो मन दुख्यो, ऊ रोयो.

examples.native: तिमीसँग कुरा गरेर मन हल्का भयो।
examples.roman: timisaṃga kurā garera man halkā bhayo.
examples.en: Talking to you has made me feel better.
I'm sorry, I made a mistake.

grammar.title: Sorry for…, thanks for…, congratulations on…: -एकोमा
grammar.body:
To say **what** you are sorry for, thankful for or congratulating someone on, Nepali adds **-मा** 'in, at' to the -एको participle: **-एकोमा** 'for having (done)'.

**Sorry:** ढिलो भ**एकोमा** माफ गर्नुहोस् 'sorry for being late'.
**Thanks:** आ**एकोमा** धन्यवाद 'thanks for coming'.
**Congratulations:** पास भ**एकोमा** बधाई छ 'congratulations on passing'.

The participle shows respect too: for तपाईं use **-नुभएकोमा** (आउ**नुभएकोमा** धन्यवाद); with a friend, plain -एकोमा. 'For **not** doing' puts न- in front: फोन **नगरेकोमा** सरी 'sorry for not calling'.

Don't confuse it with **-एकोले** (unit 14), which gives a **reason**: पानी परेकोले म आइनँ 'because it rained I didn't come'. -एकोमा names the thing you are reacting to.

A real Nepali apology is short. Between friends, **सरी यार** or **माफ गर** with a reason is plenty; **क्षमा गर्नुहोस्** and **क्षमा पाऊँ** are formal (letters, announcements, a serious wrong). Congratulations are almost always **बधाई छ!** (or 'congrats!'), often followed by a demand for a treat.

examples.en: Sorry I didn't come on your birthday.

examples.native: सबैले साथ दिएकोमा म आभारी छु।
examples.roman: sabaile sāth diekomā ma ābhāri chhu.
examples.en: I'm grateful that everyone stood by me.

dialogue.title: Failed the licence trial
dialogue.setting: Asmita has just come back from the scooter licence trial at Ekantakuna, Lalitpur. Her friend Rojan meets her at a tea shop.

lines.speaker: Rojan
lines.native: अस्मिता! के भयो? किन यस्तो उदास?
lines.roman: Asmitā! ke bhayo? kina yasto udās?
lines.en: Asmita! What's up? Why so down?

lines.speaker: Asmita
lines.native: खै यार, आज लाइसेन्सको ट्रायलमा फेल भएँ।
lines.roman: khai yār, āja lāisensko ṭrāyalmā phel bhaeṃ.
lines.en: Ugh, I failed my licence trial today.

lines.speaker: Rojan
lines.en: Oh no! At Ekantakuna? What happened?

lines.speaker: Asmita
lines.native: आठ घुम्दा खुट्टा टेकेँ। सबैले देखे, कस्तो लाज लाग्यो!
lines.roman: āṭh ghumdā khuṭṭā ṭekeṃ. sabaile dekhe, kasto lāj lāgyo!
lines.en: I put my foot down going round the figure eight. Everyone saw — so embarrassing!

lines.speaker: Rojan
lines.native: टेन्सन नलेऊ। मैले त पहिलो पटक कोन नै खसालेको थिएँ!
lines.roman: ṭensan naleu. maile ta pahilo paṭak kon nai khasāleko thieṃ!
lines.en: Don't stress. The first time, I knocked a cone over!

lines.speaker: Asmita
lines.native: साँच्चै? हाहा, तिमीले त मलाई हँसायौ।
lines.roman: sāṃchchai? hāhā, timile ta malāi haṃsāyau.
lines.en: Really? Haha, you've made me laugh.

lines.speaker: Rojan
lines.native: हो नि! अर्को पटक पास भइहाल्छौ, हिम्मत नहार।
lines.roman: ho ni! arko paṭak pās bhaihālchhau, himmat nahāra.
lines.en: Really! You'll pass next time, no problem. Chin up.

lines.speaker: Asmita
lines.native: तर फेरि फारम भर्नुपर्छ, फेरि घण्टौँ लाइन बस्नुपर्छ…
lines.roman: tara pheri phāram bharnuparchha, pheri ghanṭauṃ lāin basnuparchha…
lines.en: But I have to fill in the form again, queue for hours again…

lines.speaker: Rojan
lines.native: म तिम्रो साथमा छु। फारम भर्ने दिन म पनि आउँछु।
lines.roman: ma timro sāthmā chhu. phāram bharne din ma pani āuṃchhu.
lines.en: I'm with you. I'll come along on the day you fill in the form.

lines.speaker: Asmita
lines.native: थ्याङ्क्यु यार। अब मन अलि हल्का भयो।
lines.roman: thyāṅkyu yār. aba man ali halkā bhayo.
lines.en: Thanks, man. I feel a bit better now.

lines.speaker: Rojan
lines.native: ल, मःम खान जाऔँ। तिमी नहाँसेसम्म म छोड्दिनँ!
lines.roman: la, momo khāna jāauṃ. timi nahāṃsesamma ma chhoḍdinaṃ!
lines.en: Right, let's go for momos. I'm not letting you go until you laugh!

lines.speaker: Asmita
lines.en: OK, but today it's your treat!

culture:
Among close friends and family, Nepalis say **धन्यवाद** and **माफ गर्नुहोस्** much less than English speakers do — a formal thank-you to your best friend can sound distant, as if you were keeping score. Between friends, care is shown by turning up, teasing, feeding each other and saying **टेन्सन नलेऊ, म छु नि**. **सरी** is the everyday apology; **माफ गर्नुहोस्** is for strangers and elders; **क्षमा** belongs to letters, speeches and serious wrongs.

Exam results are a public event: when the SEE (grade 10) or university results come out, families hand out sweets and friends demand a treat (**पार्टी खोइ?** 'where's the party?'). If someone fails, people say **अर्को पटक पास भइहाल्छौ** and don't dwell on it.

When someone dies, people go to the family's home to sit with them, especially during the 13 days of mourning (**किरिया**), when the chief mourners wear white and avoid salt and many foods. Say little — **सुनेर धेरै दुःख लाग्यो**, **केही चाहिए भन्नुहोला** — and use the respectful **बित्नुभयो** 'passed away', never मर्‍यो. On social media the standard comment is **भावपूर्ण श्रद्धाञ्जली** 'heartfelt tribute' or **हार्दिक समवेदना**.

tip.title: Feelings that happen to you
tip.body:
- Many feelings *happen to* you: **मलाई** + feeling + **लाग्यो / भयो / आयो**.
- **नरमाइलो लाग्यो** 'I felt bad' · **एक्लो महसुस भयो** 'I felt lonely' · **टेन्सन भयो** 'I got stressed'.
- Missing someone: **मलाई** तिम्रो **याद आयो** — the missed person takes **-को**, and the verb stays **आयो** (it agrees with याद, not with you).
tip.pattern: मलाई + X-को याद आयो  ·  मलाई + नरमाइलो लाग्यो

tip.title: Don't worry, don't panic, don't give up
tip.body:
- To a friend (तिमी), put **न-** before the command: **नलेऊ**, **नहार**, **नरोऊ**, **नगर**.
- To someone you call तपाईं: **नआत्तिनुहोस्**, **चिन्ता नगर्नुहोस्** (fast speech: -नुस्).
- Make it warm with **न**, **है** and **म छु नि** 'I'm here'.

sentences.en: Don't worry, I'm here.

sentences.native: यार, टेन्सन नलेऊ, सबै ठीक हुन्छ।
sentences.roman: yār, ṭensan naleu, sabai ṭhik hunchha.
sentences.en: Man, don't stress, it'll all be fine.
Don't panic, the ambulance is coming.

sentences.en: So you lost once — so what? Don't give up.

sentences.native: म आत्तिएँ, तर दाइले साथ दिनुभयो।
sentences.roman: ma āttieṃ, tara dāile sāth dinubhayo.

sentences.en: Whatever happens, we're with you.

lessons.title: Until you feel better

tip.title: While, as soon as, until
tip.body:
- **-दा** 'while, when': सुन्**दा**, हुँ**दा**, गर्**दा**.
- **-ने बित्तिकै** 'as soon as': घर पुग्**ने बित्तिकै**.
- **Until** = 'as long as … *not*': **न** + -एसम्म: ठीक **नभएसम्म** 'until you're OK', **नआएसम्म** 'until he comes'.
- Don't drop the न: भएसम्म means 'as long as'.

new: केही भए मलाई फोन गर है।

sentences.en: Hearing this made me feel bad.

sentences.native: म दुःखी हुँदा तिमी सधैँ फोन गर्छौ।

sentences.en: Whenever I'm sad, you always call.

sentences.native: जबसम्म म यहाँ छु, तिमीलाई केही हुँदैन।
sentences.roman: jabasamma ma yahāṃ chhu, timilāi kehi huṃdaina.
sentences.en: As long as I'm here, nothing will happen to you.

sentences.native: तिमीसँग कुरा गर्दा मन हल्का हुन्छ।
sentences.roman: timisaṃga kurā gardā man halkā hunchha.
sentences.en: Talking with you always makes me feel lighter.

sentences.native: त्यो बेला म धेरै एक्लो थिएँ।
sentences.roman: tyo belā ma dherai eklo thieṃ.
sentences.en: At that time I was very lonely.

lessons.title: Saying sorry properly

tip.title: मबाट गल्ती भयो — and making people laugh or cry
tip.body:
- Sincere apology: **मबाट गल्ती भयो** 'a mistake happened from me'. Blunter: मैले गल्ती गरेँ.
- Add **-आउनु** to *cause* a feeling: दुख्नु → **दुखाउनु** 'hurt someone', रुनु → **रुवाउनु**, हाँस्नु → **हँसाउनु**.
- The causer is the doer, so the past takes **ले**: तिमी**ले** मलाई हँसायौ. The plain verb doesn't: मेरो मन दुख्यो.
tip.pattern: मबाट गल्ती भयो  ·  X-ले मलाई हँसायो

new: तिम्रो मन दुखाउने मेरो इरादा थिएन।

sentences.native: सरी यार, मबाट ठूलो गल्ती भयो।
sentences.roman: sari yār, mabāṭa ṭhulo galti bhayo.
sentences.en: Sorry, man, I really messed up.

sentences.native: मैले तिम्रो मन दुखाएँ, माफ गर।
sentences.roman: maile timro man dukhāeṃ, māph gara.
sentences.en: I hurt your feelings — I'm sorry.
Did what I said yesterday hurt you?
You made me laugh so much!
What she said made me cry.
I made a mistake, please forgive me. (formal)
The little brother made his sister cry.

sentences.native: मसँग नरिसाऊ न, मेरो इरादा त्यस्तो थिएन।
sentences.roman: masaṃga narisāu na, mero irādā tyasto thiena.
sentences.en: Don't be mad at me, I didn't mean it like that.
Why did my sister get angry?

tip.title: -एकोमा: 'for (having done)'
tip.body:
- **-एकोमा** names what you're sorry, thankful or happy about: पास भ**एकोमा** बधाई छ, ढिलो आ**एकोमा** माफ गर्नुहोस्.
- For तपाईं: **-नुभएकोमा**: सहयोग गर्**नुभएकोमा** धन्यवाद.
- 'For not…': **न**-: फोन **नगरेकोमा** सरी.
tip.pattern: verb-एकोमा + बधाई छ / धन्यवाद / माफ गर्नुहोस्

sentences.native: नयाँ जागिर पाएकोमा बधाई छ, यार!
sentences.roman: nayāṃ jāgir pāekomā badhāi chha, yār!
sentences.en: Congrats on the new job, man!
Sorry I didn't call.
Congratulations on your great results!
Thank you for helping me.
Sorry for being late to the meeting.
Don't be sad about failing.

sentences.native: तिमी पास भएकोमा आमा धेरै खुसी हुनुहुन्छ।
sentences.roman: timi pās bhaekomā āmā dherai khusi hunuhunchha.
sentences.en: Mum is so happy that you've passed.

sentences.native: नतिजा आयो? पास भयौ कि फेल?
sentences.roman: natijā āyo? pās bhayau ki phel?
sentences.en: Are the results out? Did you pass or fail?

sentences.native: म पास भएँ! खुसीले आँसु आयो।
sentences.roman: ma pās bhaeṃ! khusile āṃsu āyo.
sentences.en: I passed! I cried with happiness.
Come on, give me a hug!

tip.title: Condolences
tip.body:
- Use the respectful past for the person who died: **बित्नुभयो** 'passed away' — never मर्‍यो.
- Say little: **सुनेर धेरै दुःख लाग्यो**, and offer help: **केही चाहिए भन्नुहोला**.
- In writing and on social media: **हार्दिक समवेदना**.
tip.pattern: X बित्नुभएको सुनेर धेरै दुःख लाग्यो

sentences.en: His grandfather passed away last night.

sentences.native: तिम्रो बुबा बित्नुभएको सुनेर धेरै दुःख लाग्यो।
sentences.roman: timro bubā bitnubhaeko sunera dherai dukha lāgyo.
sentences.en: I was so sorry to hear your father passed away.
If you need anything, do tell me.
It's been a year since my mother passed away.

sentences.native: समय बित्दै जान्छ, मन हल्का हुन्छ।
sentences.roman: samaya bitdai jānchha, man halkā hunchha.
sentences.en: Time goes by, and the heart gets lighter.
Please pass on our condolences to his family.
We're all with your family.
Everyone sent their heartfelt condolences.
